alignments.note: מַה שֶּׁ fused in the single *Whatsoever*, which carries both the indefinite and the relative, exactly as כֹּל אֲשֶׁר does (rules 30, 35); headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme.
הָיָה with its auxiliary, headed on the lexical verb (rule 24).
כְּבָר rendered by the adverbial phrase *long ago*; headed on *long* as the word carrying the lexeme (rules 24, 31). Heading on *ago* was the competing reading.
Niphal verb with its auxiliary, headed on the lexical verb (rule 24).
Construct noun with a supplied *the* (rule 29).
Suffix → *thereof* (rule 18).
Waw → *and*.
Niphal participle recast with an impersonal frame, headed on the lexical verb (rule 24).
The complementizer אֲשֶׁר is what the ASV's *what* realizes in this recasting of *that he is man*.
The ASV's recasting *what man is* writes no pronoun for the explicit הוּא; the copula goes to the predicate under rule 20, not to the subject pronoun.
אָדָם with the construction-supplied copula (rule 20). The marginal gloss *Hebrew Adam* was read and set aside under rule 38.
Waw plus negative fused in *neither*, which carries both the coordination and the negation; headed on the negative (rule 35).
יָכֹל is what the modal *can* renders, and it keeps its subject pronoun (rules 17, 35); the negation is written separately in *neither*, so nothing is indivisible here.
The ASV writes the infinitive as a bare modal complement, *can he contend*, so the לְ has no English (rules 52, 40).
Infinitive construct → *contend*.
עִם → *with*.

The written relative שֶׁ takes *him that*, the supplied antecedent going with it, a present relative taking the English before a bare adjective does (rules 46's first rider, 41); headed on the pronoun.
Predicate adjective with the construction-supplied copula (rule 20).
Comparative מִן → *than*.
Suffix → *he* (rule 18).
